description.narrative:
Stakeholders impact:
Increased access to finance for small business owners (micro-entrepreneurs), including women borrowers: India houses approximately 17% of the worlds unbanked population at 230 million. Further, IFC estimates the MSME finance gap in India to be US$333 billion, equivalent to 13% of GDP, when including both formal and informal sectors. Noting this gap, IFC anticipates that the proposed investment will increase access to finance for the underserved MSMEs, particularly small business owners (micro-entrepreneurs) including women borrowers, thereby enabling them to expand their businesses, generate income, support families, and contribute to their economic empowerment.
Market impact:
Competitiveness: Access to credit for MSMEs, particularly for micro-enterprises, continues to remain constrained in India. IFC anticipates that this project will promote enhanced competitiveness via demonstration and replication channels, by showcasing the viability of providing financing to underserved small business owners in small towns and rural regions, including to women borrowers.

The proposed investment comprises of an IFC own account debt investment of up to INR5 billion (approximately US$60 million) in Five Star Business Finance Limited (Five Star, or the Company). The entire proceeds from IFCs investment will be utilized by the Company for growing its business loans portfolio targeting small business owners (micro-entrepreneurs) and self-employed individuals. At least 55% of the investment proceeds will be utilized by the Company for on-lending to women as primary borrowers.
